newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai calls for opening of China's gold market.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai calls for opening of China's gold market.

text.p: The Shanghai-based Business Newspaper said on Friday that it is time for China to open its strictly-controlled gold market, with supplies increasing and prices stable.
China produced a total of 108 tonnes gold in 1995 and expects an annual turnover of 150 tonnes by 2000, the newspaper said.
The price of gold in China has approached the average level in the world market, it said.
China's increasing foreign exchange reserves, which amounted to $95 billion by September, can also help to stablise the gold market, the newspaper added but gave no further details.
The current retail price of 99.9 percent pure gold in Shanghai is 141 yuan ($17) per gram.

Gold trading of all kinds is currently strictly controlled. Gold can only be sold to the state, at a price 10 percent below the state-set market price. Individuals and companies are not allowed to buy or sell gold to each other.
